doc.title: Candido Camero — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Septet versus conjunto and Arsenio Rodriguez
summary: He explains the instrumentation of a septet versus a conjunto and credits Arsenio Rodriguez with creating the conjunto around 1934.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played what: early band size and instrumentation

blocks.x: Maestro tell me the difference between the sextet and conjunto.

Well, the septet consists of seven, which are the tres, the guitar, the bass, bongos, trumpet, maracas, and clave - that's the septet. Apart from those instruments I just mentioned, the conjunto has an additional trumpet, piano, and conga. That's the difference.
Precisely. When was it that the conjunto was created? In what era did the conjunto become popular? And to some extent I guess, replaced the septet.

Exactly. Well, to my understanding it was around the year 1934 and it was the conjunto of Arsenio Rodriguez, that was when he added a trumpet which means then that he had two trumpets, conga and piano. So this means that instead of seven they were ten. So he
changed the name to conjunto because they were ten.
I estimate that this revolutionized Cuban music.
